goal: Full migration qualified for a human cutover review, not permission to switch.
boundary: Read-only evaluator. Isolated representative synthetic fixtures only. Never import a private Knowledge Root, stop services, send outbound requests or perform cutover.

evidencePolicy.authorityEnrollment: Verifier and human public keys must be enrolled independently by the native operator. Receipt-supplied keys, model reports and test-pass booleans grant no authority.
evidencePolicy.exactScope: Each legacy declaration, command, configuration, canonical operation and client scenario needs its own exact-scope signed qualification receipt with checked artifact bytes and current fingerprints.
evidencePolicy.functionalParity: Preserve all existing PKM capabilities and behavior. The explicitly approved removal of Notes/Board count and byte ceilings is an intentional relaxation, not a feature deletion or a requirement to reproduce those former ceilings.
evidencePolicy.freshness: Receipts are content-bound to the complete current implementation, inventory and readiness contract. No clock-based freshness shortcut.

nativeCatalogMap.batch21Limits: This native-composed writer is explicitly mapped to the skills workstream only to require its own signed parity evidence; it remains an unaccepted candidate. Removal requires the native-owned disposable fixture, exact actor/workspace/package source and target bindings, owner/epoch and plan approvals, ordered source/projection history and durable anchors. It removes only an existing managed lineage; mixed source/projection history is denied. Unknown partial unlink, directory removal or post-commit anchor outcomes require exact native recovery and are never startup-applied. Unix no-follow bounded UTF-8 handling is covered only in bounded fixtures. Install and remove history remains separate from the older projection journal; unrelated storage/direct-native effects require composed authority. This does not qualify hostile external-writer exclusion, OS-level locking, production authority, power-loss durability, or cutover.
nativeCatalogMap.batch22Limits: This native-composed bridge is explicitly mapped to the skills workstream only to require its own signed parity evidence; it remains an unaccepted candidate. It bridges only a strictly pinned, already-installed old Skill-source head into sequence-one native source history, retaining the immutable legacy genesis and old receipts. Independent approveBridge, verifyBridge and reconcileBridgeAnchor callbacks are required outside SQLite transactions. A removed legacy head must first be reinstalled by the old writer; direct removed-genesis bridging and broader legacy/all-target qualification are unsupported. Recognized bundled leaves remain rejected; custom-source preservation is bounded to the exercised case. Existing source/projection snapshots and database schema are unchanged. This does not qualify hostile external-writer exclusion, OS-level locking, production authority, power-loss durability, workstream acceptance, or cutover.
nativeCatalogMap.batch20Limits: This native-composed writer is explicitly mapped to the skills workstream only to require its own signed parity evidence; it remains an unaccepted candidate. Exclusive native-owned disposable fixtures require independent exact actor/workspace/package source and target bindings, owner/epoch and plan approvals, source history and durable anchors. Actual original-writer Core HTTP/MCP install, coordinated backup and fresh atomic restore/adoption, old retry/new install, rebackup and rerestore are bounded fixture tests. nativeCatalogMap.batch19Limits: Separate original-compatible preview/apply/rollback candidate, not a change to the strict classifier or acceptance of all assets. Actual original-writer result order, UUID journals, continued known-error prefixes and reverse rollback bytes are compared in exclusive native-owned disposable Unix fixtures. Native actor/epoch/genesis/history/pending callbacks are mandatory and independently checked before replay. Backup originalCompatible:true is a discriminator, not authority; independent source-manifest/root/destination-stage/history/epoch/policy/expiry adoption approval and native adoption anchors are required before staging and publication. Immutable original receipts/results/journals remain unchanged in separate adoption lineage. Mixed strict and original backup histories, unknown residue and unapproved lineage deny. No hostile external-writer lock, production authority, authority enrollment, signatures, workstream acceptance or cutover is granted. Workspace schema22 preserves prior 12–21 workspace/backup input bytes until explicit open; engine schema2 is unchanged.
nativeCatalogMap.batch16Limits: Classification remains strict whole-selection and disposable-native-fixture only, not original partial-success parity. Memory forget is derived SQLite logical erasure only, not physical or cross-engine erasure. Batch17 classified restore is available only in disposable native fixtures with separate trusted adoption approval before staging and publication, bound to actor, workspace, source identity, manifest, source epoch, destination parent, stage pins and policy identity; the immutable adoption ledger preserves original opaque receipts and publication is no-replace. This does not qualify hostile external writers, production authority, authority self-enrollment or cutover. General erased-memory backup remains unqualified; Batch18 supports only an explicitly native-owned single-workspace fixture with restored engine inside its workspace, actual writer quiescence and independent durable engineStateAuthority content seals outside both restore targets. Startup, backup and restore share read-only engine byte/table/identity validation; live/unknown effect seals cannot authorize restart. No separate target/two-root restore or automatic reconciliation is supported. Missing markers do not identify unaffected old backups.

Imported historical opaque command IDs replay only the current snapshot; project.update remains a separate strict-CAS path. The single project.legacy.command@1 operation continues to admit its previously bounded Project/Recipe command set. Batch12 separately qualifies project.recipe.trash.command@1 for explicit default-deny native move/restore authorization, strict opaque command validation, actor/workspace/source-control/database-root binding, supported canonical exports, fresh owned staging, atomic no-replace publish, schema16 intent recovery and bounded global replay. Batch13 adds a conditional native Note/Board journal bridge and bounded raw schema-1 projects.json adoption; Batch14 separately qualifies an explicit native paused-Snapshot restore and the source-bound inline Note writer; only explicit source/command scopes are supported. Snapshot resume/cancel require native actor/owner/epoch/expiry checks and human approval; unknown snapshot intents are inspect/cancel/confirm-only, and inline unknown intent requires an exact same-actor retry. Safe-state validation runs before backup/recovery effects. Schema18 preserves prior workspace/backup inputs 12–17, which migrate only on explicit open. Six selected Core HTTP/MCP reads detect observed pre/post digest changes but do not form atomic snapshots or defeat ABA. Unknown/mixed state, unsupported runtime fields, external-writer/power-loss guarantees and complete Project/Recipe parity remain unsupported or unqualified. The 28-case injected I/O matrix is bounded evidence, not an approved SLO or physical power-loss/kernel-ENOSPC qualification. Other unsupported Core controls and complete client parity remain open.

Ordered opaque deletion history is preserved; restore uses the existing knowledge.trash.restore@1 runtime receipt. Adopted entries expose list/get/restore.original/delete.original/empty.original; permanent deletion uses exact durable selection, immutable global receipts and explicit actor-authorized recovery. Unknown buckets/journals, pending locks/temp state, symlinks, tamper, collisions, outside references, secrets, Board/Memory/System/path-derived identity, unsupported Prompts/Scripts, cross-area ownership, external writers and full client behavior remain unsupported or need approved redesign; no silent exclusions. Discovery-only does not load/qualify plugins. Optional providers may be explicitly disabled by a human; outbound tests are not automatically mandatory.

policies.remaining: Actual large isolated soak with independent artifact/identity oracle, resource trend and complete failure logs. Proposed values are not approved thresholds or measurements.
Operator chooses justified workload, retention, latency/memory/queue budgets and measurement windows; no implicit SLO.
Actual isolated storage/power-loss fault qualification or explicitly scoped operator-approved equivalent fault model with limitations and independent recovery oracle; SIGKILL alone is not power-loss.

optionalOperationalGates.description: These proposed stability thresholds, fault campaigns and operating approvals are tracked separately and do not determine functional parity. They must not be reported as removed PKM functionality or silently treated as approved.
